A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe SynMotion and support comparison of the main method and experiments. However, v1 includes Appendices A-C, while v2 ends after the references despite referring to an appendix for additional comparisons and quantitative ablations. This material gap limits supplementary-content comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original T2V results in Table 1, I2V comparisons in Appendix A and Table 2, and component ablations in Table 3.

after.justification: v2 reports original generation results in Table 1 and a new study involving 20 volunteers in Table 2. Retained experimental results also qualify.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.3 retain the dual subject/motion embeddings, Zero-Conv residuals, embedding refiner, low-rank attention adapters, and SPV sampling strategy. No change to the proposed training or inference procedure is documented; the broader training data are assessed separately.

E1.justification: Section 3.4 expands reported MotionBench coverage from 16 to 26 action categories. v2 also reports training on FlexiACT's complex real-world motions and fitness exercises, extending beyond the specific animal-transfer example using FlexiAct in v1 Appendix A.3. T2V, I2V, and animal-to-animal transfer were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: The Table 1 comparator set and qualitative ReVersion comparison remain unchanged. MotionClone is newly evaluated in v2's user-study Table 2 alongside DMT, MotionInversion, and MotionDirector. Further comparator changes in the referenced but unavailable appendix cannot be verified.

E3.justification: MotionBench's stated exemplar count changes from 6-10 to 20 videos per action. v2 adds CLIP-T, two FVD variants, and Flow Score, plus a protocol involving 20 volunteers rating 20 groups of five methods on three criteria. These substantially extend evaluation; the PDFs do not establish that the retained scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: The qualitative component ablation in Figure 5 is retained. v1 additionally provides quantitative ablations in Appendix B.1/Table 3 and failure analyses for backflips and missing body parts. v2 still refers to appendix ablations but supplies no appendix, preventing verification of whether these analyses were retained or revised.

E5.justification: v2 first reports ± values for Flow Score and user-study percentages. Their statistical meaning and estimation procedure are not defined in the supplied file. The existing statement that QwenVL evaluation is repeated ten times per motion remains unchanged; additional independent training runs are not established.

E6.justification: All seven original Table 1 metric columns retain their numerical values. v2 adds substantial results, including SynMotion's CLIP-T of 0.322, FVD values of 212.05 and 3129.19, and Flow Score of 0.41±0.02. New user-study preferences are 78.3%, 81.9%, and 83.9% for motion alignment, subject alignment, and video quality. These additions do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, dual-embedding residual equations, and low-rank adapter formulation remain mathematically unchanged. The added evaluation metrics introduce no formal definitions, derivations, or proofs in the supplied v2.

C1.justification: Both versions claim joint semantic and visual motion customization, subject-motion disentanglement, SPV-supported training, MotionBench, and strong T2V/I2V performance. The abstract's revised superiority wording does not materially strengthen the claim because v1 already claims state-of-the-art performance in its introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: The main interpretations of baseline weaknesses and component roles remain substantially unchanged. v1's appendices discuss complex-motion failures, insufficient body-part visibility, multiple moving entities, and disagreement between VLM metrics and human perception. The absent v2 appendix prevents establishing whether these qualifications were retained or substantively revised.

D1.justification: Available implementation information retains 2,000 AdamW iterations, learning rate 2e-5, sampling probability 0.75, eight H20 GPUs, and the same project link and planned code release. However, v1's detailed I2V embedding and concatenation instructions have no supplied appendix counterpart in v2, leaving the full extent of reproducibility-documentation changes unresolved.

R1.justification: v2 refreshes citations, adding works such as MotionClone, PhysMaster, MemFlow, LayerFlow, and LongCat-Video and removing others such as Ming-Omni and Ranni. The central semantic-versus-visual taxonomy and positioning of SynMotion as a hybrid approach remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose are retained, with localized condensation and wording edits. Authors and affiliations change, acknowledgments and a user-study paragraph are added, and Section 4.3 changes from More Results to Generalization on I2V. The available main text is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the paper into two columns, moves the teaser to the first page, redraws Figure 2 horizontally, expands Table 1, and adds a user-study table. v1 Figure 7 is retained as v2 Figure 6; v1's separate celebrity-results Figure 6 is absent. The appendix figures and tables are also unavailable in v2.

improvement.justification: The user study and additional quantitative metrics strengthen empirical assessment. However, v2 does not clarify whether the unchanged original scores use the enlarged MotionBench, and its new ± values lack statistical definitions. Its absent appendix also prevents checking I2V comparisons, quantitative ablations, implementation details, and limitations available in v1. These gains and verification gaps do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
